capital_structure_note: CRITICAL: KMD.NZ underwent a 1-for-0.73 accelerated renounceable entitlement offer + placement (NZ$65.3m gross at NZ$0.06/share, 47.1% discount to TERP) in March/April 2026, roughly doubling the share count from 711.7m to ~1,799.5m, followed by a 1-for-25 share consolidation effective ~June 2026 reducing the count to ~72.0m. The Metrics.csv SharesOutstanding column (711.667m at FY2025) is PRE-RAISE and PRE-CONSOLIDATION and must NOT be used for current valuation -- 72.0m is used throughout this DCF. All per-share history (EPS, DPS, book value per share) before the raise/consolidation is NOT comparable to current per-share figures. Yahoo Finance has back-adjusted historical prices by the ~25x consolidation ratio; this DCF's historical EV/EBITDA sanity check un-adjusts those prices (divides by 25) and applies the actual historical (pre-raise) share count at each date to reconstruct genuine historical EV -- it does NOT mix adjusted prices with the current 72.0m share count for historical years.

inputs.shares_outstanding_note: Post-raise, post 1-for-25 consolidation (~June 2026). CSV's 711.667m figure is stale/pre-raise -- do not use.
inputs.net_debt_note: Pro-forma bank debt (ex-IFRS16 lease liabilities) at Jan-2026 after applying net equity raise proceeds, per company disclosure. Reported net debt at Jan-2026 was NZ$94.0m pre-raise. IFRS16 lease liabilities (~NZ$287.9m at H1-2026) are excluded from net_debt because lease costs are handled via the lease-principal deduction from owner FCF (Step A), not via the capital structure -- capitalizing leases in both net_debt AND deducting lease principal from FCF would double-count.
inputs.interest_income_note: FY2025 interest income was only NZ$2.772m against net DEBT (not net cash) of ~NZ$52.8m reported / NZ$31.9m pro-forma -- KMD is a net debt company, so no interest-income double-count risk exists; not stripped.
inputs.sbc_source: 10-K/Annual Report FY2025 cash flow statement (Employee share-based remuneration, NZ$391k) -- confirmed small, no buybacks in any year FY2021-2025 (ShareRepurchases = 0 each year per kpis table)
inputs.uncovered_dilution_note: Zero buybacks in any year FY2021-2025; company just completed a massively dilutive rescue raise. SBC is fully uncovered and dilutes the share count, though the dollar amounts are small (<NZ$1.5m/yr even at Y10) relative to the ~NZ$126m market cap, so the dilution effect is modest (<1.5%/yr).
inputs.annual_share_growth_pct_note: Approximated flat 1.0%/yr from uncovered SBC dilution.
inputs.lease_treatment_note: KMD is a store-network retailer reporting under IFRS 16. Reported OCF/FCF is inflated because lease payments split into financing (principal, ~NZ$93.3m FY2025) and operating (interest) -- the principal portion never appears as a deduction from OCF. Owner FCF = reported_fcf - lease_principal_repayment - SBC (interest income immaterial, not stripped). FY2025: reported FCF NZ$101.6m -> owner FCF NZ$7.9m after this adjustment.
inputs.working_capital_note: FY2024/FY2025 reported FCF was further boosted by non-repeatable inventory liquidation (inventories NZ$303.7m Jan-25 -> NZ$274.1m Jan-26, management's 'third successive year' of reduction toward 'optimal levels'). H1-2026 already shows this reversing: a NZ$21.3m working-capital OUTFLOW as sales grow. The forward projection therefore treats working capital as a USE of cash proportional to revenue growth (wc_capture 15% base case), the opposite sign to the historical tailwind.

historical_growth.eps_cagr_note: EPS CAGR not meaningful -- KMD reported statutory NET LOSSES in FY2024 (-$48.3m) and FY2025 (-$93.6m); no valid CAGR can be computed off negative base/end values.
historical_growth.fcf_cagr_note: FCF CAGR not meaningful on either reported or owner-FCF basis -- owner FCF was NEGATIVE in FY2022 (-$34.2m) and the series (FY2020 $72.8m -> FY2025 $7.9m) is a collapse, not a compounding growth series.
historical_growth.growth_rate_source: NONE -- historical CAGRs are not used as the forward growth driver for this name. Revenue growth (~2.5-5.5% base case p.a.) and EBIT margin recovery are instead anchored to management's H1 FY2026 run-rate (+7.3% YoY sales), the FY2026 trading update, and the 'Next Level' FY28 targets (60% gross margin, 10% underlying EBITDA margin), tempered to reflect only partial/mid-cycle success given the group's repeated history of unmet strategic resets. See valuation_philosophy.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Revenue 3yr CAGR (~0.3%) and Equity 3yr CAGR (~-6.7%) diverge sharply -- both confirm this is NOT a compounder: revenue is roughly flat over the cycle while shareholders' equity has been consistently eroded by net losses (Oboz impairments, weak trading). Neither is used as the forward growth anchor; see growth_rate_source.

underlying_ebitda_history.FY2026_guided: 31.5-34.0 (management guidance, per Analysis JSON trading update -- not independently verified in Extracted/ filings, which only go to H1 FY2026)

mid_cycle_ebitda_analysis.note: Underlying EBITDA (management's own non-GAAP measure) EXCLUDES the impact of IFRS 16 (i.e. is presented on a pre-lease-capitalization, rent-as-opex basis) plus restructuring, impairment, onerous contracts, SaaS accounting and notional amortisation of customer relationships. It is NOT the same basis as the CSV's statutory EBITDA column (FY2025: $50.5m stat vs $17.7m underlying) because statutory still includes the IFRS16 uplift. This DCF does NOT build off underlying EBITDA directly -- it instead anchors on STATUTORY (IFRS16-inclusive) EBIT margin, which is a more basis-stable metric (H1 FY2026 statutory EBIT -$1.7m vs underlying EBIT -$6.4m -- much closer than the EBITDA lines), then adds back statutory D&A (including ROU depreciation) to reconstruct an IFRS16-consistent 'owner EBITDA' figure for the terminal exit-multiple cap, keeping the multiple-basis internally consistent with the historical EV/statutory-EBITDA multiples computed in the sanity check (2.1x-3.3x).
mid_cycle_ebitda_analysis.mid_cycle_selection: Base case ramps statutory EBIT margin from ~0% (FY26E, consistent with H1 FY26 actual of -0.3%) to a MATURE 6.0% by Year 10 -- well below the FY2021 peak (10.0%, a COVID-stimulus/pre-tariff bounce) and below FY2023 (6.9%), and materially short of management's own FY28 'Next Level' target trajectory (10% underlying EBITDA margin, which on a statutory/IFRS16 basis would likely translate to a statutory EBIT margin above 6%). This reflects the view that Rip Curl -- the former profit engine, now the weak link with -2.8% same-store sales and -13% EBITDA in the July 2026 update -- only partially recovers, and that KMD's track record of repeated unmet strategic resets (multiple CEOs, cost programs) warrants skepticism about full target achievement. Bull case reaches 9.5% (full 'Next Level' success); bear case reaches only 2.0% (turnaround stalls).

base.wc_capture_note: Applied as a USE of cash on revenue growth (working capital REBUILDS as sales recover, reversing the FY24/25 inventory-liquidation tailwind) -- opposite sign convention to a typical growth company.
base.cash_tax_rate_note: Ramps from 15% (Y1, reflecting NZ/AU tax-loss carryforwards from FY2024/25 losses) to a normal 28% blended AU/NZ corporate rate by Y5.
base.terminal_cap_multiple_basis: Statutory (IFRS16-inclusive) EBITDA, matching the historical EV/EBITDA range computed in the sanity check (2.1x-3.3x, avg 2.7x). Base uses the ~2.7x average.

bull.narrative: 'Next Level' strategy succeeds close to management's FY28 targets; Rip Curl stabilises under new CEO Ashley Reade; Kathmandu momentum sustains; leverage <0.5x achieved ahead of schedule de-risking WACC to 15%; strategic review outcome (potential brand divestment) not modelled as a discrete one-off but reflected via a lower WACC and top-of-range 3.3x exit multiple.

bear.narrative: Rip Curl decline continues unchecked, Kathmandu momentum fades once easy comps cycle through, Oboz tariff pressure persists, no brand divestment materialises, execution risk on repeated strategic resets proves out -- turnaround stalls near breakeven with WACC remaining elevated (19%) on continued covenant/execution risk.

stack.component: NZ/AU small-cap base cost of capital
Extreme cyclicality / operating leverage (underlying EBITDA fell >6x peak-to-trough, $113.3m FY21 to $17.7m FY25, in 4 years)
Recent covenant stress / dilutive rescue raise / going-concern-adjacent leverage history (3.8x net debt/EBITDA at Jan-2026)
Weather + consumer-discretionary + fashion/inventory risk, three-brand execution complexity
US tariff exposure (Oboz 82% USA, Rip Curl US ~12% of group sales)

base.note: Entry price ($2.19) sits ABOVE base intrinsic value ($1.87) because base-case WACC (17%) exceeds the 15% IRR hurdle -- discounting the same projected cash flows at a lower rate mechanically produces a higher present value. This is the same pattern documented for CDI.NZ: when WACC > hurdle, entry price is correctly above IV, not below it.

sensitivity.basis: Base-case revenue/margin/tax/lease assumptions held constant; only WACC and terminal growth vary. Exit multiple cap (2.7x statutory EBITDA) held constant.

sanity_check.historical_multiple_basis: Historical EV/EBITDA reconstructed by UN-ADJUSTING Yahoo's ~25x consolidation-adjusted historical prices (divide by 25) and applying the ACTUAL historical (pre-raise, pre-consolidation) share count at each fiscal year-end (e.g. FY2025: 711.667m shares) -- never mixing adjusted price with the current 72.0m count.
sanity_check.trip_check: NOT TRIPPED. Base-case implied P/B (0.180x) is essentially identical to the market's current P/B (0.168x) -- both reflect deep, consistent distress-pricing of Rip Curl/Oboz goodwill and brand intangibles rather than a modelling error. Base-case implied EV/FY25-statutory-EBITDA (3.29x) sits at the top of, but within, the 6-year historical range (2.13x-3.33x) -- reasonable given FY2025 EBITDA was itself the cycle trough, so a higher-than-average multiple applied to a depressed base is expected, not anomalous. Implied exit multiples in all three scenarios (bear 0.68x, base 1.31x, bull 2.48x) are all BELOW the historical range, confirming terminal value is NOT assuming multiple expansion -- if anything the model is conservative on exit pricing relative to KMD's own trading history.
sanity_check.diagnosis: The market is pricing KMD.NZ (P/B ~0.17x) consistent with continued distress / minimal recovery. The DCF's base case, built on a genuinely disciplined mid-cycle EBIT margin (6.0% statutory by Y10, well short of both the FY21 peak of 10.0% and management's FY28 aspiration), lands almost exactly where the market already sits (+6.7% upside) -- i.e. the base case is NOT a bull thesis, it largely validates the market's current distressed pricing. The real spread in this name is not base-vs-market but bull-vs-bear (+241% vs -89%), driven overwhelmingly by whether the 'Next Level' turnaround succeeds and/or the strategic review crystallises Rip Curl's residual sum-of-parts value (acquired for ~A$350m/NZ$378m in 2019 against a CURRENT GROUP EV of only ~NZ$158m for all three brands combined).
sanity_check.fix_applied: None required -- multiples check out on both sides (P/B and EV/EBITDA) without adjustment.

valuation_philosophy: KMD Brands is treated as a distressed/turnaround cyclical retailer, not a compounder -- historical revenue CAGR is ~flat (0.3%/yr over 3 years) and equity CAGR is NEGATIVE (-6.7%/yr), so neither is used as a forward growth anchor (see historical_growth.growth_rate_source). Three structural choices drive this valuation: (1) OWNER FCF deducts full IFRS16 lease principal repayment (~NZ$93.3m FY2025, ~9.4% of revenue) from reported FCF -- reported FCF ($101.6m FY2025) is a statutory-accounting artefact that flatters cash generation for a store-network retailer, and owner FCF collapses to just $7.9m once this and the small SBC charge are removed. (2) MID-CYCLE, not trough or peak, statutory EBIT margins are used, ramping from ~0% (matching the H1 FY2026 actual of -0.3%) to a genuinely conservative 6.0% by Year 10 -- deliberately well short of both the FY2021 COVID-bounce peak (10.0%) and management's own FY28 'Next Level' target (10% underlying EBITDA margin), because KMD has a multi-year track record of unmet strategic resets and Rip Curl (56% of sales, the former profit engine) is currently DECLINING (-2.8% same-store sales, -13% EBITDA YoY per the July 2026 trading update). (3) TERMINAL VALUE is capped at KMD's own historical EV/statutory-EBITDA trading range (2.13x-3.33x, avg 2.71x, computed by un-adjusting Yahoo's consolidation-adjusted prices against actual historical share counts) rather than a Gordon-growth perpetuity at any premium multiple -- apparel/footwear retail with no structural moat does not warrant one. In every scenario Gordon growth (at a high 15-19% WACC, reflecting genuine micro-cap illiquidity, extreme cyclicality and recent covenant stress) binds below the exit-multiple cap, so the model is not assuming multiple expansion. The RESULT is that base-case intrinsic value ($1.87, +6.7%) lands almost exactly where the market already prices the stock (P/B 0.18x model vs 0.17x market) -- the base case validates rather than challenges the market's distressed pricing. The genuinely wide bull ($5.97, +241%) / bear ($0.19, -89%) spread instead reflects the real optionality in this name: a sum-of-the-parts view where Rip Curl alone cost ~A$350m (~NZ$378m) to acquire in 2019 against a CURRENT GROUP enterprise value of only ~NZ$158m for Kathmandu, Rip Curl AND Oboz combined -- a gap the live strategic/portfolio review (concluding at the 23-Sept-2026 FY26 results, an explicit binary catalyst per management's own guidance) could crystallise via a brand divestment, or could equally validate as 'the brands genuinely earn their depressed multiple' if Rip Curl's decline continues and no divestment eventuates. Probability weights (25% bull / 50% base / 25% bear) are applied honestly rather than skewed toward either extreme, given the binary, unresolved nature of the FY26 outcome.

corporate_action_flag.description: Strategic/business review of the brand portfolio (assessing divestment of 'non-core assets') is targeted to conclude at the FY2026 full-year results on 23-September-2026 -- a real, near-term binary catalyst not otherwise reflected in the DCF's cash-flow projections.
